sentences.text: Allegations in brief are that, many farmers from Sompura village of Nelamangala Taluk and Devanahalli have made claim petitions for compensation before the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (for short the KIADB) pertaining to the acquisition of their respective lands.
Accused persons at the instance of officials and officers of KIADB have approached those farmers who applied for the compensation.
They have assured farmers to ensure the release and payment of their respective compensations at the earliest by influencing the officers and officials on commission basis.
Accused persons took the signed blank cheques and other documents including agreements from farmers as a security towards the commission amount.
They have received the commission amount from various farmers falsely stating as if it is because of their efforts, the compensation amount came to be released and thereby cheated the farmers.
According to 6 Spl. C.C.678/2020 the prosecution, accused No.1 to 9 have committed afore stated offences.
3. Accused No.1 to 9 being in the custody of the police having represented through their respective counsel were got enlarged on the bail.
Subsequently, the police have filed the charge sheet before this court against accused persons in respect of aforestated offences.
After complying the mandate as contemplated under Section 190(1)(b) of Cr.P.C., this court has got registered the case.
Copies of the charge sheet were furnished to accused persons.
In the mean time, the 5th accused was discharged by the order of this court dtd.22.8.2022.

My predecessor in office has framed charges against accused No.1 to 4 and 6 to 9 for offences punishable under Sections 7(A) of the PC Act r/w.
Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, read over and explained the same in the language known to them.
They have pleaded not guilty.
As they claims to be tried, the trial of the case has been fixed.
4. To prove its allegations, the prosecution has examined Pw.1 to 36 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to P41.
After closure of the prosecution evidence and getting compliance under Section 437(A), the statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. has been recorded and explained the same to accused persons.
They denies the incriminating circumstances appearing against them.
They have not adduced any evidence.
Their defence is the total denial of the prosecution's case to be false.
5. Heard arguments from both side.

6. Points for consideration are :
1. Does the prosecution prove beyond all and 6 to 9 have committed the offence punishable under Section 7(A) of the PC Act r/w. Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code?
2. What order?

sentences.text: The SLAO2 is one of the signatory to the search panchanama at Ex.P3.
Therefore, her version in the cross examination that, she had no information about the brokerage activities in her office and not personally seen them etc. assumes no meaning.
Being aware of these realities, the I.O. has cleverly ignored the allegations of the corrupt activities facing by the KIADB officials and the huge amount found unofficially in their possession.
In other words, his efforts to protect the KIADB officials stands substantiated by his acts of giving clean chit to them and declining to collect the crime related evidence.
The following evidence of the I.O. at para8 is one such instance which exposes his intention of giving protection to the corrupt officials.

18. The circumstances emanating from the above discussion gives no scope to justify acts of the I.O.
in 17 Spl. C.C.678/2020 returning the amount and cite those officials as prosecution witnesses so generously rather than pointing out their involvement in the corrupt activities as rightly argued by the learned Public Prosecutor.

In this way, the I.O. himself has defeated the very purpose for which the report at Ex.P19 in the form of the complaint submitted by Pw.16, the object behind the registration of the case and the raid conducted.

19. After giving the clean chit to the corrupt officials of the KIADB, the I.O. has for the name sake charge sheeted only the private persons in respect of offences punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7(A) of the PC Act.

The language employed under Section 7(A) of the PC Act makes clear that, the acceptance or obtainment of an undue advantage by a person from another person as a motive or reward to influence the public servant by corrupt or illegal means to perform the public duty improperly or dishonestly is an essential requirement to attract the offence.
In other words, the involvement of both the public servants and other than public servants together in corrupt activities is a matter of necessity to constitute an offence.

Here the evidence to that extent gets eroded with the acts of the I.O. in giving clean chit to the accused on the one hand and his failure to effective investigation in the matter of collecting the related evidence on the other hand.
Obviously no material 18 Spl. C.C.678/2020 on record to attract the offence under Section 7(A) of the PC Act against accused persons in the absence of public servants as accused.

Admittedly, the 1st accused Sri. Siddagangappa, the 2nd accused Sri. Siddalingappa and the 3rd accused Sri. Renukeshwara were not at all present in the KIADB office on the day of the raid.
Even nothing has been recovered from them despite separate searches deposed to have conducted by the I.O. in their houses except the unrelated 7 documents from the house of the 2 nd accused.
There exists no material or reasons for the I.O. to implicate them in the case as rightly argued by the learned defence counsel.

At the same time, the seizure of Rs.1,45,000/ from the 5th accused,
Rs.7,17,000/ from the 8th accused, Rs.11,200/ from the 9th accused in the KIADB office at the time of raid is not in dispute.
22.

Though the learned defence counsel have cross examined the I.O. and disputed the involvement of these accused persons with the KIADB officials in the corrupt activities, they have not denied that, Rs.7,17,000/ recovered from the 8th accused belongs to the SLAO2.

Moreover,
neither the 8th accused nor the 5th and 9th accused have explained as to the necessity of carrying the huge amount to the KIADB office if really it belongs to them.

Under circumstances and for reasons discussed above, I am to agree with the learned Prosecutor that, the 20 Spl. C.C.678/2020 said amount being an illegal gratification kept with these accused persons by the KIADB Officials including the SLAO2 after collecting it from the public.
Perhaps this is the reason for the respective accused in declining to put forth their claim upon the amount till date.

On the strength of the above observations I am to hold that, no further discussion is a matter of necessity to indicate the failure of the prosecution to bring home the guilt of accused persons in respect of alleged offences beyond all reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, point No.1 is answered in the negative.
23. Before penning down, I may be wrong if I do not make remarks as against the illegal acts of KIADB officials so also impropriety committed by the I.O. in this case.
The factual discussion herein before unfurls the corrupt activities on the part of the KIADB officials.
The undeclared lakhs of rupees unofficially found in their possession on the day of raid is the clear evidence therefor.

The purpose of maintaining the attendance register, movement register and cash declaration register in the public offices is to avoid the corrupt activities and ensure the transparency in discharging the official duties.
But the failure to maintain the cash declaration register by the SLAO2 in the office is the serious lapse on her part.

Possessing lakhs together of rupees unofficially not only by her but also officials who were working in the said office is 21 Spl. C.C.678/2020 the best instance to understand the depth of corruption and modus operandi they have adopted to encourage the related activities with the help of agents.

The office of the KIADB is known for the corruption wherein, the general public particularly the farmers who lost their lands and approaches for compensation are becoming the real victims at the hands of the officials.
The observations made in this judgment reveals the uncontrollable business atmosphere in the KIADB rather than the atmosphere of an official functions.

sentences.text: 24. Unambiguously the I.O. has ignored and destroyed the visible crime related evidence on the one hand and failed to gather the crucial evidence during his investigation on the other hand.
He strived to protect the officials rather than pointing out their involvement in the corrupt activities.
His acts of simply charge sheeting the private individuals i.e. accused No.1 to 9 to the exclusion of the public servants under the PC Act is most unfortunate.
I find no hesitation to say that, there exists no reasons for the I.O. to give go bye to the officials and cite them as prosecution witnesses.
This kind of mischievous approach does not bear any meaning but 22 Spl. C.C.678/2020 reveals the injustice caused by him to the society at large apart committing the impropriety to his position.
In other words, the worst investigation carried out by him in the case is the best example of as to how the investigating officer has escaped the corrupt officials for reasons known to him.
Therefore, he shall be held responsible for the same so also the false implication of accused No.1 to 3 in the case, and acquittal of other accused persons.
25. This is not the first time for the court to observe this kind of worst investigations in many cases.

Where, the officers are dare enough even to file B reports in the trap cases, giving go bye to the main accused / influential officers ignoring the direct allegations, the involvement in the crime and charge sheeting the subordinate officials for the name sake, knowingly obtaining the prosecution sanction orders from the authorities not competent to accord and so on.
Many of such cases pending on the file of this court ultimately ended and still ending in acquittal.

In the light of the above, I am to express that, deputing or posting of welltrained, honest and competent police officers particularly to the Lokayukta police wing, SIT, CCB and CID is a matter of an absolute necessity to ensure the effective investigations and subject the real culprits to justice.
Otherwise, mere registration of hundreds of cases for different offences for statistics purpose would not serve the real purpose.
I mean to say that, such cases results in 23 Spl. C.C.678/2020 injustice rather than ensuring the justice to the society at large.
Office is hereby directed to forward the copy of this judgment to the Hon'ble Karnataka Lokayukta for the kind information.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Accused No.1 to 4 and 6 to 9 being the private individuals are facing allegations in respect of offences punishable under Section 7(A) of the PC Act and Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
Thus obviously, the failure of SLAO2 to ensure the declaration of cash by the officials including herself is evident to understand the modus operandi they have adopted to encourage the corrupt activities in the office.
they have thereby buried the transparency in the office.
Therefore, virtually the dereliction of duty on the part of the SLAO2 and the officials who were working under her as on 15.10.2019 is unambiguous.
This kind of conduct on the part of the public servants is very shocking as it is an indication of corrupt activities.
Being aware of these realities, the I.O. has cleverly ignored the allegations of the corrupt activities facing by the KIADB officials and the huge amount found unofficially in their possession.
In other words, his efforts to protect the KIADB officials stands substantiated by his acts of giving clean chit to them and declining to collect the crime related evidence.
In this way, the I.O. himself has defeated the very purpose for which the report at Ex.P19 in the form of the complaint submitted by Pw.16, the object behind the registration of the case and the raid conducted.
19. After giving the clean chit to the corrupt officials of the KIADB, the I.O. has for the name sake charge sheeted only the private persons in respect of offences punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7(A) of the PC Act.
The language employed under Section 7(A) of the PC Act makes clear that, the acceptance or obtainment of an undue advantage by a person from another person as a motive or reward to influence the public servant by corrupt or illegal means to perform the public duty improperly or dishonestly is an essential requirement to attract the offence.
In other words, the involvement of both the public servants and other than public servants together in corrupt activities is a matter of necessity to constitute an offence.
The purpose of maintaining the attendance register, movement register and cash declaration register in the public offices is to avoid the corrupt activities and ensure the transparency in discharging the official duties.
But the failure to maintain the cash declaration register by the SLAO2 in the office is the serious lapse on her part.
Possessing lakhs together of rupees unofficially not only by her but also officials who were working in the said office is 21 Spl. C.C.678/2020 the best instance to understand the depth of corruption and modus operandi they have adopted to encourage the related activities with the help of agents.
The office of the KIADB is known for the corruption wherein, the general public particularly the farmers who lost their lands and approaches for compensation are becoming the real victims at the hands of the officials.
He strived to protect the officials rather than pointing out their involvement in the corrupt activities.
His acts of simply charge sheeting the private individuals i.e. accused No.1 to 9 to the exclusion of the public servants under the PC Act is most unfortunate.
This kind of mischievous approach does not bear any meaning but 22 Spl. C.C.678/2020 reveals the injustice caused by him to the society at large apart committing the impropriety to his position.
Therefore, he shall be held responsible for the same so also the false implication of accused No.1 to 3 in the case, and acquittal of other accused persons.
Where, the officers are dare enough even to file B reports in the trap cases, giving go bye to the main accused / influential officers ignoring the direct allegations, the involvement in the crime and charge sheeting the subordinate officials for the name sake, knowingly obtaining the prosecution sanction orders from the authorities not competent to accord and so on.
In the light of the above, I am to express that, deputing or posting of welltrained, honest and competent police officers particularly to the Lokayukta police wing, SIT, CCB and CID is a matter of an absolute necessity to ensure the effective investigations and subject the real culprits to justice.
Otherwise, mere registration of hundreds of cases for different offences for statistics purpose would not serve the real purpose.
